- Model consistently overestimates prices in the early part of the 30-day horizon, especially after recent spikes; reduce initial forecast values by 0.5–1.5% for the first 5–7 days.
- After a price spike, model tends to overshoot and then overcorrect — apply a dampening factor (e.g., 0.95 multiplier) to the peak forecast values to avoid excessive volatility.
- When sentiment is neutral (all 0.00), model exhibits strong upward bias — adjust forecast by subtracting 1.0–2.0% from the mean of the 30-day forecast to account for lack of bullish sentiment.
- Mean reversion is evident in later days — if forecast is >1.5% above recent 7-day average, reduce by 0.3–0.7% per day until convergence.
- Horizon-specific error: 30-day forecasts often overpredict late-period prices (days 20–30) — cap forecast at 1.0–1.5% below the 30-day moving average of true outcomes for days 20–30.
